topic: Testing and validation in iterative development

findings.message: slide 10: the text snippet was not checked (no checker for 'text' on this machine); read it before teaching

slide 3 ('Recap: Software factories & trace analysis'): [fact] The claim that execution traces capture every step is too absolute, since practical traces are often sampled, truncated, or omit internal tool and model details. Fix: Say that execution traces record the observable steps and events of an agent run, subject to the logging configuration.

slide 6 ('Test types generated by agents'): [fact] The table's qualitative ratings of agent support for property-based, mutation, contract, and stress testing are unsupported and may vary substantially by tool and domain. Fix: Remove the High/Medium/Low ratings or label them explicitly as illustrative and tool-dependent.

slide 7 ('Validation strategies'): [fact] The note says static analysis catches syntax/type errors, but syntax errors are normally rejected by the compiler or interpreter before static analysis runs. Fix: Say that static analysis catches type, lint, and semantic issues, while syntax errors are usually caught earlier by the compiler or parser.

slide 10 ('Worked example: Identify three failure causes'): [fact] The 401 authentication failure is not explicitly mapped to a failure category, although it is the clearest evidence of a logical error in the generated code in this example. Fix: Include the 401 assertion failure as evidence of a logical error in generated code, while noting that the missing API key may also contribute.

evidence.title: Worked example: Identify three failure causes

findings.message: slide 10 ('Worked example: Identify three failure causes'): [clarity] The worked example does not explicitly show how the WARN configuration line is distinguished from the specification mismatch, dependency conflict, and resource exhaustion categories. Fix: State that the missing API key is configuration drift and explain why the 401 assertion alone does not establish its root cause.

evidence.title: Worked example: Identify three failure causes

findings.message: slide 11 ('Hands‑on: Analyze a 2000‑line agent log'): [clarity] The activity requires students to run a parser script and apply clustering without specifying the script, log format, or clustering method, so students may not be able to reproduce the stated workflow consistently. Fix: Provide the parser and clustering script, the log schema, and the expected clustering parameters or output format before the activity.

slide 12 ('Check: Failure category matching'): [quiz] The question is not fully unambiguous because a missing required configuration value can also be treated as a specification mismatch, although the explicit SpecParser error makes option 0 the intended answer. Fix: Ask which line explicitly reports a parser-level specification validation failure, or state that the answer must be the line explicitly labeled SpecParser.

slide 15 ('Tooling: log parsers & visualization'): [fact] Vector is described as an open-source log parser, but it is primarily a general-purpose observability data pipeline and log-processing agent rather than a dedicated parser. Fix: Describe Vector as a log-processing and observability pipeline, and list dedicated parsing tools such as Logstash separately.

slide 16 ('Integrating analysis into CI/CD pipelines'): [other] Automated rollback on critical regressions is presented as a standard CI/CD capability even though it requires application-specific deployment and rollback mechanisms and can be unsafe for irreversible changes. Fix: State that rollback should be triggered only when a tested, application-specific rollback mechanism and safety policy are available.

slide 17 ('Key takeaways'): [fact] The takeaway says there are three common categories but lists five categories, contradicting the taxonomy on slide 9. Fix: Change the bullet to five common categories: specification, configuration, dependencies, resources, and logic.
